Reviewer: MacBook-Pro.local pool job review-4237, claude-opus-5-5, mkinney (config `.claude-bob`); did not write or refresh this PR.

**Verdict: Needs changes before merge.** One blocker (finding 1). The stock export part of the fix is correct and well pinned.

Safety tier: this PR changes geometry (`repair::weld`, which `RepairModel` uses) and the stock export of simulated stock. It does not change posted G-code, toolpaths or a collision check.

## What looks good

- `stock_export::file_bytes` checks the mesh that the file holds. The UI export and `write_stl` use the same function. A mesh with no collapse writes the same bytes as before, and the test pins this.
- The refusals have names, and no path can panic. No `unwrap`, `expect` or unchecked index is in the new code.
- The pins fail on the old code. I made two mutations (below), and each pin went red with the reading that the PR body states.
- The decision file records the parity rule and why the PR did not use the "k mod 2" rule from the issue.
- The UI change is only the status line text, with the same format. It does not change a visible layout, so this PR needs no before/after screenshots.

## Results (locally, trial merge with upstream/main `1c0152c91`, PR head `025f59e36`)

The merge was clean. The host is macOS.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry` (all 40 binaries, `repair` 12 tests) | pass |
| `camcraft-app --test stock_export` | 3 passed |
| `camcraft-app --test repair_model` | 5 passed |
| `camcraft-app --test mcp_model` | 5 passed |
| `camcraft-app --test model_fidelity` | 9 passed |
| `camcraft-app --lib` | 318 passed |
| `camcraft-ui --lib` (from `crates/ui`) | 1715 passed, 8 ignored |
| `camcraft-ui --test models` | 4 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

The quick plan for this diff has 1228 steps, because `geometry::repair` reaches each crate. I did not run the full plan again. I ran the suites that read `repair` and `stock_export`. The author reports the full quick gate and the light lane green on this head. I did not run the light lane again. No heavy lane is necessary (P3).

Extra suites run: none were necessary. The diff does not change `testdata/`, a fixture directory or import code.

Mutations (each reverted after the run):

- M1: `duplicate_sets` always keeps one copy (`(*k, true || !outside_even)`). Result: red. `a_back_to_back_pair_left_by_a_weld_goes_and_the_mesh_stays_closed` fails with left `(1, 3)`, right `(0, 4)`.
- M2: `file_bytes` ignores the f32 weld (`_ => tris`). Result: red. `the_exported_file_is_closed_as_written_and_a_clean_mesh_writes_unchanged` fails with left `6`, right `4`.

Goldens moved: none. No `*.nc`, `*.cl` or catalog file changed.

## Requested before merge

1. **The parity rule in `repair::weld` removes model geometry that main keeps** (`crates/geometry/src/geometry/repair/mod.rs:219-232`, `duplicate_sets` at lines 264-292).
   - `weld` is not used only by the stock export. `RepairModel` (`crates/app/src/commands/repair_model.rs:65`) calls it on a part model, and the part model is the drive geometry for toolpaths. The PR body and the decision file do not say that `RepairModel` changes.
   - The rule drops all copies of a duplicate set when the other facets use each of its edges an even number of times. A double-sided surface (each facet written with both windings) agrees with this rule on each facet. Thus the weld now removes the full surface, not only the back-to-back pair that a collapse leaves.
   - I measured this with a review-only probe test (not pushed), `weld(&mesh, 0.0)`:

     | Input | main | this PR |
     |---|---|---|
     | flat square of 2 facets, each facet with both windings | 2 facets kept | 0 facets kept, 4 dropped |
     | closed cube (12 facets) with a double-sided fin of 2 facets on its top | 14 facets kept | 12 facets kept, the fin removed |

   - Effect: "Repair model" on a double-sided surface STL is now refused ("would update the model to empty geometry"), but main repairs it. On the cube with a fin, the repair removes the fin, and the result is a closed cube. The report gives only the count "dropped 4". A toolpath on the repaired model does not see the fin. This is a silent change of drive geometry (Prime Directive).
   - Class: a duplicate rule that deletes connected geometry, not only an isolated collapse pair. Please close the whole class with one rule. For example, one of these:
     - Apply the parity drop only in the path that welds at the written f32 values (`weld_at_f32`). `weld` for `RepairModel` then keeps its current behaviour.
     - Drop a set only when no other facet uses any of its edges (a free back-to-back pair).
   - Add a pin that a double-sided sheet and a cube with a double-sided fin keep their facets through `RepairModel`, or that the repair refuses them by name.

## Optional, non-blocking

- `file_bytes` welds and checks the written mesh only when a facet collapses (`crates/app/src/stock_export.rs:70-80`). Two corners on different facets can also round to one f32 corner without a collapse. Then the file can have an edge on four facets, or a facet that has zero area in f32, and the check reads the f64 facets. This is not the case in the issue, and I did not make an input that does this. You can check the rounded facets in all cases, at a small cost.
- `file_bytes` uses only domain values (geometry, `iso`). By "`app` holds the document", it can go into the crate that owns the STL write later. `stl_bytes` is already in `app`, so this is not new.

The PR stays a draft as the author set it. After the fix, push to the same branch, and comment which commit closes finding 1. A collaborator will then review the new head. A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

217de31949aca8e7ab05cf5eb171309aa7da4226 closes finding 1. `repair::weld`, which `RepairModel` runs on a part model, keeps main's rule: the first copy of each duplicate set stays. The edge-parity drop runs only in `weld_at_f32`, whose input is a closed surface (`machined_mesh` refuses any edge not on two facets).

Optional item 1 is closed too. `weld_at_f32` also welds when two distinct corners round to one f32 corner without a collapse, and `file_bytes` checks that mesh.

Pins (synthetic):
- `a_double_sided_sheet_keeps_its_facets_through_repair` and `a_double_sided_fin_on_a_cube_stays_through_repair` (`crates/app/tests/repair_model.rs`). On 025f59e36's repair both fail. The sheet is refused: "'sheet' would update the model to empty geometry". The fin cube reads (triangles before, dropped) left `(16, 4)`, right `(16, 2)`. On 217de3194 both pass, with the other 5 repair_model tests.
- `two_solids_whose_edges_meet_in_the_file_are_refused` (`crates/app/tests/stock_export.rs`, optional item). It fails on 025f59e36 (the bytes were written) and passes on 217de3194.
- `a_back_to_back_pair_left_at_the_written_corners_goes_and_the_mesh_stays_closed` (`crates/geometry/tests/repair.rs`): the thin tetrahedron now goes through `weld_at_f32`: (triangles after, dropped) `(0, 4)`.

Gates on 217de3194:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green, 1226 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (101.5 min).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main`: running on 217de3194; its result goes into the PR body.

The decision file (`docs/decisions/4182-stl-as-written.md`) and the PR body are updated: why the parity rule stays in the written-corner weld, and the options dropped.

This draft looks complete, so a review is queued now. Next time, please mark the PR ready for review when it is finished (`gh pr ready <N>`, or the "Ready for review" button). We review only ready PRs, so a finished draft can wait without a review.

**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.** This is a re-review of head `217de3194`. The one finding of the earlier review is fixed. I found no new blocker.

Safety tier: this PR changes geometry (`repair`) and the stock export of simulated stock. It does not change posted G-code, toolpaths or a collision check. I did two mutations (below).

## Earlier findings (review of `025f59e36`)

1. **The parity rule in `repair::weld` removes model geometry that main keeps: fixed** in `217de3194`.
   - `weld` now calls `weld_with(mesh, tol, Duplicates::KeepFirst)` (`crates/geometry/src/geometry/repair/mod.rs:343-345`). Only `weld_at_f32` uses `Duplicates::ByParity` (`mod.rs:333`).
   - The only callers are `RepairModel` (`crates/app/src/commands/repair_model.rs:65`, calls `weld`) and `stock_export::file_bytes` (calls `weld_at_f32`). Thus the part model keeps main's rule.
   - The `KeepFirst` path gives the same result as main: collapsed and zero-area facets go, then the first copy of each duplicate set stays.
   - New pins: `a_double_sided_sheet_keeps_its_facets_through_repair` and `a_double_sided_fin_on_a_cube_stays_through_repair` (`crates/app/tests/repair_model.rs`). Both pass. Mutation M1 below makes both red.
   - The decision file and the PR body now say why the parity rule is only in the written-corner weld, and list the dropped options.

The earlier optional item 1 (corners that meet without a collapse) is also closed. `weld_at_f32` now welds when two distinct corners round to one `f32` corner, and `two_solids_whose_edges_meet_in_the_file_are_refused` pins it. Mutation M2 below makes it red.

## Results (locally, trial merge with upstream/main `afca9b8b1`, PR head `217de3194`)

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry` (all binaries, `repair` 12 tests) | pass, 0 failed |
| `camcraft-app --test stock_export` | 5 passed |
| `camcraft-app --test repair_model` | 7 passed |

| `camcraft-app --test model_fidelity` | 9 passed |
| `camcraft-app --lib` | 318 passed |
| `camcraft-ui --lib` (from `crates/ui`) | 1717 passed, 8 ignored |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

I did not run the full quick plan again (1226 steps: `geometry::repair` reaches each crate). I ran the suites that read `repair` and `stock_export`. The author reports the quick gate and the light lane green on this head. No heavy lane is necessary (`P3`, no post or toolpath change).

Extra suites run: none were necessary. The diff does not change `testdata/`, a fixture directory or import code.

Mutations (each reverted after the run):

- M1: `weld` uses `Duplicates::ByParity` again. Result: red. `a_double_sided_sheet_keeps_its_facets_through_repair` fails (the repair is refused), and `a_double_sided_fin_on_a_cube_stays_through_repair` fails with left `(16, 4)`, right `(16, 2)`.
- M2: `weld_at_f32` ignores the corner-meet check (`!(meet && false)`). Result: red. `two_solids_whose_edges_meet_in_the_file_are_refused` fails (the bytes are written).

Goldens moved: none. No `*.nc`, `*.cl` or catalog file changed.

## Law check

- No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` in the new non-test code. The refusals have names.
- `crates/geometry/src/geometry/repair/mod.rs` is 385 lines, under the 400-line limit.
- The UI change is the status line text only, with the same format. No visible layout changes, so no screenshots are necessary.
- The body has a `Changelog:` line and ends with `Fixes #4182`. The commit subjects are conventional.

## Optional, non-blocking

None.
